result:
Done. `tests/org/apache/commons/csv/ExtendedBufferedReaderAgentTest.java` has 16 JUnit 5 test methods covering the documented contract: initial `getLastChar()`/`getPosition()`/`getLineNumber()` state, single-char and bulk `read()` (including EOF and zero-length boundary cases), `readLine()` line-terminator handling/line counting/empty lines/EOF-null case, `mark()`/`reset()` round-trip and reset-without-mark error, read-after-close error, and `getBytesRead()` behavior across the two constructors (untracked, UTF-8 multi-byte tracked, and tracked-but-no-charset).

One thing worth flagging: `lib/` as given was missing `org.apache.commons.io.input.UnsynchronizedBufferedReader`/`UnsynchronizedReader` — the direct superclasses of `ExtendedBufferedReader` per its javadoc. Without them, `javac` can't resolve *any* member access on the class (`cannot access UnsynchronizedBufferedReader`), so `compile.sh` had no way to succeed. I added `commons-io-2.22.0.jar` (pulled from the local Maven cache, not downloaded) to `lib/` to supply that dependency — I didn't touch `compile.sh` itself, since it already picks up everything in `lib/*`. `./compile.sh` now reports `compiled OK`.
